paper_id: Ni et al. - 2003 - ANDMARC Indoor Location Sensing Using Active RFID
title: LANDMARC: Indoor Location Sensing Using Active RFID
venue: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications (PerCom)
motivation: GPS fails indoors; existing indoor solutions (infrared/802.11/ultrasonic) suffer from line-of-sight, cost, or accuracy issues.
problem_framing: Can commodity RFID technology enable cost-effective indoor location sensing despite not being designed for it?
key_insight: Use extra fixed reference tags as calibration landmarks; comparing signal strength patterns between reference and tracking tags compensates for environmental dynamics.
method_signature: k-nearest neighbor using Euclidean distance in signal strength space, weighted by inverse-square E value.
evaluation_criteria: Location error e = linear distance between real and computed coordinates; analyzed via cumulative percentile distributions.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: First reader-coverage approach failed: even static objects reported in different sub-regions due to dynamics; higher tag density improvement less than expected.
evidence_for_taste: optimization problem turns out to be useless
even a static object could be reported in different sub-regions
the improvement is not as great as we expected
error due to dynamics of environment can hardly be alleviated
such an error is often unpredictable
thinking_moves: 先证现有方法失效: 证明基于读者覆盖子区域的优化问题无法工作
将定位问题重新框架为模式匹配: 比较参考标签与跟踪标签的信号强度模式
利用环境干扰的对称性: 参考标签与跟踪标签受相同环境影响
经验调参确定超参数: 通过实验选择k=4最优值
